item: 5. Auto-vs-human stats conclusions + FOV unit of replication
evidence: FOV UNIT CONFIRMED IN CODE: cohort() builds per-run `runs`, then fov = runs.groupby(['fov','mouse']).mean() (runs sharing a FOV averaged first); significance via wil() = scipy.wilcoxon over fov[col] (n = #FOVs, labelled level=FOV); state_dependence Wilcoxon over FOV rows; dendrite/depth coupling via statsmodels mixedlm(..., groups=fov) (random intercept per FOV); compare() computes wilcoxon_p_fov = wilcoxon over FOV means (fa = m.groupby('fov').mean()). The only run-level number is spearman_across_runs, an explicitly-labelled method-agreement descriptor, not a biological significance test. => No t-tests, and no significance test treats runs sharing a FOV as independent replicates. Summaries: auto 20 runs/10 FOVs, human 17 runs/9 FOVs. CONCLUSIONS AGREE: mean_pairwise_r (both sig>0: human .051/auto .025), frac_pairs_significant (both 14%), corr_vs_distance (both sig negative), dimensionality (both low PR/N .20/.13), global_events (both FOV-specific .15/.10), same_fov_reproducibility (.49/.53), global_coupling_pupil (both NS), global_coupling_whisker (both sig+), dendrite_coupling_accel (both sig+), global_coupling_accel (both sig+), state_dependence (both: event rate higher when moving, pair r NS), depth_vs_event_rate (both NS). CONCLUSIONS DIFFER (transparently reported, scientific caveat not code bug): dendrite_coupling_pupil (human sig NEGATIVE r=-0.047 p=.011 vs auto NS +0.022 p=.43; median_r_pupil sign flips, p_diff .016), dendrite_coupling_whisker (auto sig+ r=.068 p=.0075 vs human NS .026 p=.46), accel_onset_global_ca (auto sig p=.039 vs human NS p=.078, marginal), depth_vs_amplitude (auto strong+ coef .077 p=4.6e-6 vs human NS -0.032 p=.32). These divergences are flagged in compare_auto_vs_human.txt and are inherent to auto finding ~3-4x more/finer units; the comparison methodology itself is sound.
